# CruiseMapper Sailing Search by Destination & Date

Search CruiseMapper's public cruise database by destination, ship, cruise line, date, length, theme, and price, and get back one structured record per sailing with departure date, route, nights, and starting price.

## What this actor does

- Searches cruise sailings by any combination of destination region, cruise theme, date range, length, cruise line, ship, departure port, and port of call
- Accepts full CruiseMapper search URLs directly, merging and deduplicating their results with any other filters you set
- Caps results by a minimum and maximum starting price and a maximum number of records
- Jumps directly to the first result page for a future departure date, so a date far beyond today still returns sailings instead of walking page by page
- Can enrich each unique ship in the results with its own specifications (year built, tonnage, passenger capacity, cabins, and more)
- Leaves out any field a sailing doesn't have, such as a starting price the cruise line hasn't published, rather than returning it empty

## Output per sailing

- `departureDate`, `departureDateText` — parsed ISO date and the original date text as shown on the page
- `daysUntilDeparture` — days from now until departure; negative for past sailings
- `shipName`, `shipUrl` — vessel name and its CruiseMapper detail page
- `duration` — cruise length in nights
- `routeType` — `round-trip`, `one-way`, `open-jaw`, or `transatlantic`, when CruiseMapper's own listing states it
- `title` — the cruise itinerary's title
- `priceFrom`, `currency` — starting price, when the cruise line has published one
- `shipDetails` — present only when ship enrichment is turned on: `yearBuilt`, `builder`, `shipClass`, `flagState`, `speed`, `lengthMeters`, `beamMeters`, `draftMeters`, `grossTonnage`, `passengerCapacity`, `crewCount`, `deckCount`, `cabinCount`, `decksWithCabins`, `engines`, `owner`, `operator`, and other specs CruiseMapper publishes for that ship
- `scrapedAt`

When a search matches no sailings at all, the run finishes with a single informational record instead of an empty, silent dataset.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `departureFrom` | string | – | Earliest departure date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); defaults to today if left empty, so past sailings are dropped |
| `endDate` | string | – | Latest departure date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); no upper bound if left empty |
| `cruiseLength` | string (select) | `any` | `any`, `1-2`, `3-5`, `6-10`, `11-14`, or `15+` nights |
| `destination` | string (select) | `any` | Destination region, e.g. `alaska`, `mediterranean-black-sea`, `bahamas-caribbean-bermuda`, `nile-river` |
| `cruiseType` | string (select) | `any` | Cruise theme, e.g. `transatlantic`, `christmas`, `food-wine`, `panama-canal` |
| `shipName` | string | – | Ship name, matched as a substring, e.g. `Symphony of the Seas` |
| `cruiseLine` | string | – | Cruise line, e.g. `Royal Caribbean`, `Carnival` |
| `departurePort` | string | – | Embarkation port, e.g. `Miami`, `Barcelona` |
| `portOfCall` | string | – | An intermediate port the cruise must stop at, e.g. `Cozumel` |
| `maxPrice` | integer | `10000` | Drop sailings with a starting price above this amount, in USD (100-100000) |
| `minPrice` | integer | `0` | Drop sailings with a starting price below this amount, in USD (0-100000). Unpriced sailings are dropped when set above 0 |
| `maxResults` | integer | `50` | Hard cap on sailings returned (1-500) |
| `enrichWithShipData` | boolean | `false` | Fetch each unique ship's own detail page and add a `shipDetails` block |
| `startUrls` | array | `[]` | Full CruiseMapper search URLs to run alongside the filters above |

### Example: Alaska cruises this summer, 6-10 nights

```json
{
  "departureFrom": "2026-06-01",
  "endDate": "2026-09-30",
  "cruiseLength": "6-10",
  "destination": "alaska",
  "maxResults": 100
}
```

### Example: a specific ship, enriched with ship specs

```json
{
  "shipName": "Symphony of the Seas",
  "enrichWithShipData": true,
  "maxResults": 20
}
```

### Example: budget Caribbean sailings from Miami

```json
{
  "destination": "bahamas-caribbean-bermuda",
  "departurePort": "Miami",
  "maxPrice": 1500,
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

## Use cases

- Feeding a travel-planning tool with current cruise inventory for a destination
- Tracking starting-price trends for a specific ship, cruise line, or route over time
- Comparing what different cruise lines charge for similar itineraries
- Building a "cruises departing this month from <port>" content digest
- Cross-referencing ship specifications (capacity, tonnage, cabins) against sailing options

## Limitations

- CruiseMapper's search results do not publish the cruise line in each row, so records identify the ship (with its ship URL) rather than the line.
- The public listing is a sailing summary, not a full day-by-day itinerary; port-by-port call times are not exposed here.
- Starting prices are shown only for the sailings where the cruise line publishes them. Unpriced sailings are omitted from price fields rather than guessed.
- One search query examines at most 200 result pages (about 3,000 rows). Narrow broad searches with destination, length, port, ship, line, or price filters to reach deeper result sets.
- `maxResults` is capped at 500 per run.

## FAQ

**Do I need a proxy or cookies?**
No — CruiseMapper's search results are public, and this actor doesn't require either.

**Why is `priceFrom` missing on some sailings?**
A meaningful share of CruiseMapper listings don't publish a starting price, usually because the cruise line requires a direct inquiry. When no price is published, the field is simply left out rather than shown as empty.

**How many results can one run return?**
Up to `maxResults`, capped at 500. For a date far in the future, the actor skips directly to the first relevant result page.

**Can I fetch full ship details for every result?**
Yes — turn on `enrichWithShipData`; each unique ship across your results is fetched once and attached as a `shipDetails` block.

**Why is `routeType` sometimes empty?**
CruiseMapper only labels a sailing's route type in its title for some cruises. When the title doesn't carry a recognizable route-type prefix, the field is left out.

**What happens if my filters match nothing?**
The run still completes successfully with a single record explaining that no sailings matched, instead of silently returning an empty dataset.

**Can I combine a pasted search URL with the filter fields?**
Yes — `startUrls` and the filter inputs run together, and the combined results are deduplicated. A `page` value inside a pasted URL is ignored so the actor can paginate from the first matching page.

**Do old CruiseMapper input keys still work?**
Yes. Older saved tasks that send `startDate`, `maxPriceUsd`, `minPriceUsd`, `maxItems`, `minNights`, or `maxNights` are read and mapped in code.

**Is this affiliated with CruiseMapper?**
No. This is an independent actor that reads CruiseMapper's publicly accessible search pages.
